title: Sandbox stdout/stderr output cap

requirement.rule: An over-budget stream keeps both ends, not one: the retained payload is the first `(max_bytes * 3) // 4` UTF-8 bytes followed by the last `max_bytes - (max_bytes * 3) // 4` bytes (48 + 16 at a budget of 64), spliced together by exactly the marker `"\n[[curator:elided {dropped} bytes]]\n"`, where `{dropped}` is the decimal count of bytes actually discarded — original size minus retained size, not original size minus `max_bytes` — with no thousands separator. The marker is charged outside the budget, so the returned text is longer than `max_bytes` by exactly the marker's length; retained bytes never include the marker.
requirement.scope: The budget is applied to the UTF-8 encoding, and both slices are pulled back to codepoint boundaries before decoding: try trimming 0, 1, 2 then 3 trailing bytes off the head and 0, 1, 2 then 3 leading bytes off the tail, taking the first candidate that decodes cleanly; only if nothing within three bytes decodes (genuinely invalid UTF-8, not merely a split codepoint) fall back to decoding the untrimmed slice with `errors="replace"`. A clean multi-byte input therefore never yields `"�"`, and the retained byte count may land below `max_bytes`.
requirement.failure_behavior: `max_output_bytes == 0` is the sentinel for *unlimited*: the whole stream comes back unshortened, unmarked and unlisted, and it does not raise even though 0 is below the floor. Any other budget under 16 (`MIN_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES == 16`) — including negatives, which reach the capping layer when it is called directly rather than through the pydantic-validated config — raises `OutputCapError`, a subclass of `ValueError`, carrying the offending value on an attribute named `max_bytes`. That check runs before the input stream is inspected at all, so a `None` stream with a budget of 8 raises rather than returning.
requirement.observability:
Through the fake seam, with a sandbox returning `stdout="0123456789" * 10, stderr="", exit_code=0` and `max_output_bytes=64`: `output.stdout == "012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567" + "
[[curator:elided 36 bytes]]
" + "4567890123456789"`, i.e. `len(output.stdout) == 93` (64 + 29), strictly greater than the budget, with the 29-character marker at offset 48. With `stdout="€" * 10` (30 bytes) and `max_output_bytes=20`: `output.stdout == "€€€€€
[[curator:elided 12 bytes]]
€"` — exactly six `€`, `"�" not in output.stdout`, retained bytes 18 rather than 20. With `stdout="A" * 300` and `max_output_bytes=0`: `len(output.stdout) == 300` and `output.truncated_streams == []`. `pytest.raises(OutputCapError)` for `max_output_bytes=15`, `1` and `8`, with `exc.value.max_bytes` equal to the value passed and `isinstance(exc.value, ValueError)`; the class is importable as `bespokelabs.curator.code_executor.output_cap.OutputCapError`; `max_output_bytes=16` does not raise.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: A stream at or under the budget is returned byte-identical with no marker; `None` is preserved as `None` rather than coerced to `""`, and `""` stays `""` — neither is reported as shortened.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: The team first reserved the notice inside the budget (`len(text.encode()) <= max_bytes` always) and reported `original - max_bytes` as the dropped count; that was reversed when the reserved-room arithmetic kept making the head shorter than the ratio implied.

requirement.rule: Capping happens at every one of the four `CodeExecutionOutput` constructions inside `_execute_in_sandbox` — the success return, the `exit_code == 124` timeout return, the non-zero-exit return, and the `except Exception` handler — rather than once where `result.stdout` / `result.stderr` are first read, and not downstream in `execute_request` or in `base_backend.handle_single_request_with_retries`. A run that produced megabytes of stdout and then blew up while leaving the sandbox still returns capped stdout.
requirement.scope: In the `except Exception` branch the streams are salvaged with `getattr(result, "stdout", None)` off a possibly half-built result; those values go through the same cap, and a salvaged `None` stays `None` in the returned output instead of becoming `""`. `files` is left alone at every site no matter how large the archive string is.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: On the non-zero-exit path the value handed to `_format_exit_code_error` is the capped stderr text, not `result.stderr` — otherwise the full stderr still ships unbounded inside `error`. `_format_exit_code_error` itself is untouched (same signature, same message text); only its input changes, so `error` ends with the identical shortened text that `output.stderr` carries, marker included.
requirement.observability:
Fake sandbox with `exit_code=1, stdout="", stderr="E" * 80` and `max_output_bytes=64`: `output.error == "Program exited with status code 1

Error details:
" + output.stderr` and `len(output.error) == 143` (a blind cap of only the stderr field gives 130). Fake sandbox whose `execute_command` returns `exit_code=0, stdout="A" * 300, stderr=""` but whose `__exit__` raises `RuntimeError("boom")`: `output.message == "error"`, `output.error == "boom"`, `len(output.stdout) == 94`, `output.stdout.endswith("A" * 16)`, `output.truncated_streams == ["stdout"]`, `output.stderr == ""` (capping only at the read site leaves 300 here). Fake sandbox with `exit_code=124, stdout="A" * 300`, `timeout=7`: `output.message == "timeout"`, `output.error == "Execution timed out after 7s"`, `len(output.stdout) == 94`.

hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: Capping was originally done once in `execute_request` on the returned `CodeExecutionOutput`; that was reversed after the exit-code error message was found to still carry the whole stderr.
